points.text: The `Verified:` line is not a valid proof. I replayed `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and got `Ran 10 tests ... OK`, the same as the PR. But neither `tests/test_cli.py` nor `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`, and the PR adds no test. The command does not test any detail the entry states: one name per line, no distance, no count line, and unchanged output without the option. The stamp (`verified: by process:pilot-dev`, `verifiedCommit: 4f9e2ab`) therefore cannot stand. Add tests that run the CLI with `--names-only`. They should check that each line is only a place name, that there is no distance and no count line, and that the output without the option is unchanged. Then replace the `Verified:` line with a command that runs those tests and gives its result. Only files under `wiki/` changed since 4f9e2ab, so that part of the stamp is fine.

No test-first history. The PR adds `--names-only` in `cli.py` with no test at all, so there is no failing-test commit before the implementation, as the TDD requirement expects. The new tests need to be committed so they show a red state against the implementation, or the history needs to show them leading the change. The `Summary` and `Closes #72` also say nothing about the behavior shipped, which is a minor gap compared with the missing tests.

The `Verified:` line does not prove the entry. It replays `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, and I re-ran it: 10 tests pass. But no test in `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`, so the command would pass with or without the feature. The entry states three details that nothing tests: one name per line, no distance and no count line, and unchanged output without the option. Add CLI tests that cover each detail, then re-stamp the entry with a proof that replays them, for example `python -m unittest tests.test_cli` once those tests exist. Until then, remove the stamp and keep `specified`. Moving an entry to `implemented` with a proof that does not test it is not accepted.

The PR adds no tests for new behavior, so the TDD requirement (a failing-test commit before the implementation commit) cannot have been met. Add the tests described above. The history should show the failing tests first, then the `cli.py` implementation that makes them pass. A regression test that the output is unchanged without `--names-only` is needed because the option sits in the same output path.

The stamp on `names-only` cannot stand. The `Verified:` line replays `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. I re-ran it and got OK (10 tests), but no test in the suite passes `--names-only`, and this PR adds none. The command passes whether or not the option works, so it does not test what the entry states: one name per line, no distance, no count line, and unchanged output without the option. Fix: add tests that exercise the entry's details, then give a `Verified:` line whose command runs them. The tests must cover three cases: with `--names-only` the output is one name per line with no distance and no count line; without the option the output is identical to before; the case with several results. If no command can prove the entry, remove the stamp (`wiki set --clear-stamp`) and use a `not by command` line with a reason that holds. A stamped entry moved to `implemented` needs its proof replayable.

TDD was not followed, and the behavior has no test coverage. The PR adds a CLI option in `cli.py` with no failing-test commit before the implementation, and no tests at all. Add CLI tests in `tests/test_cli.py`, committed as a failing test first and then the implementation, so the history shows red then green. The two guards on the entry are the most important cases to cover: no distance and no count line with the option, and unchanged output without it.

No test exercises `--names-only`. `tests/test_cli.py` and `tests/test_search.py` never pass the option, and the PR adds none. I re-ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests` on the branch and got 10 tests, OK. That result would be identical without this PR's change, so it proves nothing about the feature. Add CLI tests that check: (a) with `--names-only` the output is exactly one place name per line; (b) it has no distance and no count line; (c) without the option the output is unchanged.

The `Verified:` line and the stamp do not hold. The line only reports that the whole suite passes. That command does not test what the entry states (names only, no distance, no count line, output unchanged without the option), so the stamp (`process:pilot-dev`, commit 4f9e2ab) cannot stand. Once the tests above exist, rewrite the `Verified:` line to a command that runs them, for example `python -m unittest tests.test_cli` or the specific test names, and restamp. Until then, remove the stamp (`wiki set --clear-stamp`) and do not move the entry to `implemented`.

TDD is not shown. The PR has no failing-test commit followed by the implementation, because it has no test at all (see the first point). Put the new tests in a commit before the `cli.py` change, or at least make the history show red then green.

The `Verified:` proof does not test the entry. `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes (I re-ran it: 10 tests, OK), but no test in `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`. The command would pass without the feature, so the stamp (`process:pilot-dev`, `4f9e2ab`) is not backed by a proof. Add tests that exercise the entry in every detail it states: one place name per line, no distance, no count line, and output unchanged without the option. Then replace the `Verified:` line with a command that runs them and re-stamp the entry.

The PR adds no tests, so there is no failing-test commit before the implementation commit. TDD was not followed (`.pilot/pilot-task-implement.md` step 3). Add the tests in a commit that fails without the `cli.py` change, then keep the implementation commit after it. If the history was squashed, restructure it so the red-then-green order is visible.

The stamp does not hold. The `Verified:` line replays `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, and I got the same result (10 tests, OK). But no test in `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`, and the PR adds none. The command therefore passes with or without the feature and tests nothing the entry states: one name per line, no distance, no count line, and unchanged output without the option. Fix: add CLI tests for these behaviors, then replace the `Verified:` line with a command that runs them, for example `python -m unittest tests.test_cli`. Keep the stamp only if that run passes and only `wiki/` files changed since the stamped commit. Otherwise clear the stamp with `wiki set --clear-stamp`, and do not move the entry to `implemented` until the behavior is tested.

TDD was not followed. The PR adds no test, so the history has no failing-test commit before the implementation. The `--names-only` branch in `cli.py` is unexercised, as is the guarantee that the default output is unchanged. Add the tests as a failing-test commit followed by the implementation, or at least add tests that fail when the option is broken, such as one asserting no distance and no count line in the output.

The `Verified:` line cannot stand. Its command, `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, passes (I re-ran it: 10 tests, OK), but no test in `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`, and the PR adds none. The command therefore does not test what the entry states: one name per line, no distance, no count line, and unchanged output without the option. Add CLI tests that cover each of these details, then replay the command and put the result in the `Verified:` line.

The entry is stamped (`verified: process:pilot-dev`, `verifiedCommit: 4f9e2ab`) and moved to `implemented` on a proof that does not test it. Only `wiki/` changed since 4f9e2ab, so the stamp's commit rule holds, but the proof rule fails. Once the new tests exist, re-stamp at the commit that contains them. If the tests are not added, keep the entry at `specified` and remove the stamp.

The PR changes behavior in `cli.py` without a test, and the history shows no failing-test commit before the implementation, so TDD was not followed (`.pilot/pilot-task-implement.md` step 3). Add tests in `tests/test_cli.py` for `--names-only` and for the unchanged default output. Commit them so the history shows a test that fails first, then the implementation that makes it pass.

The `Verified:` stamp does not stand. The PR's proof is `python -m unittest discover -s tests → OK (10 tests)`. I replayed it and got the same result, but no test in `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_search.py` passes `--names-only`, so the command does not test the entry. The entry states three things: one name per line, no distance and no count line, and unchanged output without the option. Add tests that run the CLI with `--names-only` and assert those three behaviors. Then point the `Verified:` line at a command that runs them. Until a proof like that exists, do not move `names-only` to `implemented` and do not stamp it. Return it to `specified` and clear the stamp with `wiki set --clear-stamp`.

TDD was not followed. The PR adds no test and `cli.py` gains behavior with no failing-test commit before it. Add the tests as a failing-test commit ahead of the implementation commit. Cover `--names-only` output with no distance and no count line, and the default output staying the same. The history must show test-first. If the existing commits cannot show that, add the tests as a separate commit and say so in the PR body.

No test covers `--names-only`. `tests/test_cli.py` and `tests/test_search.py` never pass the option, and the PR adds none. I re-ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and it passes (10 tests), but none of them exercises the new behavior. Add CLI tests for: (a) with `--names-only`, one name per line and nothing else, with no distance and no count line; (b) without the option, the output is unchanged. This is the same gap as the missing failing-test commit. The history shows no red test before the implementation, so TDD was not followed. Add the tests, and make sure the history shows them failing before the cli.py change.

The `Verified:` stamp does not hold. The proof command `python -m unittest discover -s tests` replays to the same OK result, but it does not test what the entry states: no test calls `--names-only`, so the command would pass without the feature. The PR moves the entry to `implemented` and stamps it `process:pilot-dev` at commit 4f9e2ab on that proof. Once the tests exist, use a command that runs them (for example the specific test module or test ids) in the `Verified:` line, and re-stamp. Until then, leave the entry unstamped.

The `Verified:` line (`python -m unittest discover -s tests → OK (10 tests)`) does not test the entry. No test in tests/test_cli.py or tests/test_search.py passes `--names-only`, and the PR adds none. The same 10 tests pass with or without the feature, so the proof cannot show that the output is one name per line with no distance and no count line, or that the output is unchanged without the option. The stamp (`process:pilot-dev`, commit 4f9e2ab) and the move to `implemented` are not accepted. Fix: add CLI tests that run with `--names-only` and check exact output (names only, one per line, no distance, no count line). Also add a test that the output without the option is unchanged. Then replay them as the `Verified:` command and re-stamp.

The history shows no failing-test commit before the implementation, because no tests exist for the feature. TDD was not followed. Add the tests as a red commit followed by the implementation, or at least tests that demonstrably fail without the change.

The edge cases are untested: an empty result, and the combination of `--names-only` with the step-free filter and the distance sort. The entry says there is no count line, so an empty result should print nothing. Cover these in the new tests.
